Its readers in the source are all non-gameplay: AncientEventModel.GenerateInitialOptionsWrapper's DebugOption swap (AncientEventModel.cs:198-202) and the dev console's AncientConsoleCmd (AncientConsoleCmd.cs:41, 71), both dev tooling, plus NRelicCollectionCategory.cs:116, the relic-collection UI screen. GenerateInitialOptions builds its own list and never consults it. NARROWED IN THE REVIEW FIX PASS: the earlier wording called the DebugOption swap its "only reader", which is the over-broad negative this stream's own lesson #4 warns about -- `grep -rn AllPossibleOptions src` returns two more readers. Neither moves the verdict. NeowsBones.cs:33 reads `ModelDb.Event<Neow>().AllPossibleOptions`, hard-coded to NEOW's list, so it is not a reader of this unit's -- which is exactly why event/neow records ITS AllPossibleOptions as a real faithful function (events/neow.py:64-72) and every other ancient waives it. NRelicCollectionCategory is a compendium display. So the waiver stands on the presentation clause, now on an accurate reader list. Same treatment as event/nonupeipe's AllPossibleOptions.

CalculateVars.rationale: presentation only (dialogue). Vakuu.cs:49-57 sets the 'Visits' DynamicVar from `SaveManager.Instance.Progress.AncientStats[Id].GetVisitsAs(Character.Id) + 1`, and nothing in the source reads that var back as game state: `grep -rn '"Visits"' src` returns exactly the three Vakuu.cs sites that create it (the key const at :17, the CanonicalVars declaration at :23, this write at :55) plus one save-serializer entry for the unrelated AncientCharacterStats.Visits property. A DynamicVar with no code reader is a localization substitution token -- it exists to be interpolated into the line Vakuu speaks. The dialogue SELECTION does not read it either: AncientDialogueSet.GetValidDialogues (AncientDialogueSet.cs:104-135) matches AncientDialogue.VisitIndex against a `charVisits` argument its caller supplies, not against this var. It is also wrapped in LocalContext.IsMe, so it is per-local-player on top of that. Out of scope per the shared contract's 'presentation/dialogue' waiver. RE-GROUNDED IN THE REVIEW FIX PASS: the earlier rationale waived this as "out of scope: profile metadata", which is not one of the four permitted waiver categories (multiplayer, presentation, ascension, potions) and so read as a rule-3 violation against event/welcome_to_wongos, which files the SAME unported SaveManager.Progress dependency as a dormant GAP. The distinction is real and it is about the consequence, not the dependency: at welcome_to_wongos Progress.WongoPoints feeds a RELIC GRANT (WelcomeToWongos.cs:113-123 awards the Wongo Customer Appreciation Badge), which is game state, so the unported profile save is recorded there as a dormant gap with a named observable. Here the identical dependency terminates in a spoken line and produces nothing a run can read. Same unported thing, filed once where it has an observable; waived here on the presentation clause, not on a 'profile metadata' category that does not exist.

guards.what: UNIT GAP (dormant): Distinguished Cape's -9 Max HP is implemented on the EVENT OPTION instead of on the relic. DistinguishedCape.cs:29-31's AfterObtained() runs `CreatureCmd.LoseMaxHp(..., DynamicVars.HpLoss = 9, isFromCard: false)` and only then adds the 3 Apparitions; Vakuu.cs:38's `.ThatDecreasesMaxHp(9m)` is NOT the effect -- EventOption.cs:194-197 shows it is only `ThatWillKillPlayerIf(p => p.MaxHp <= value)`, the red-flash predicate. events/vakuu.py:52-63 `_cape_option` applies the loss itself, and relics/distinguished_cape.py:21-26's after_obtained adds only the Apparitions
guards.issue: The relic docstring (relics/distinguished_cape.py:8-11) states the placement as fact -- 'The -9 Max HP comes from the Vakuu event OPTION ..., not the relic itself' -- and it is FALSE, the fourth instance in this stream of a load-bearing sim comment asserting something the source contradicts. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes_b.py cape`): at 80/80, run.add_relic('distinguished_cape') on its own leaves the player at 80/80 with 3 Apparitions where the game leaves them at 71/71 with 3 Apparitions; the Vakuu CAPE option reaches 71/71, so the Vakuu path itself COINCIDES and this is a placement defect, not an arithmetic one. DORMANT, with the concrete trigger named and executed: the same probe shows distinguished_cape is Ancient rarity and is NOT in the relic grab bag, and `git grep distinguished_cape sts2_rl` returns only events/vakuu.py, its own relic module and vocab.json -- so the Vakuu option is the only grant path in the sim today. ANY second path (a relic reward, a shop, the grab bag, another Ancient's pool, a recording-driven resync that reconstructs the relic list) silently drops 9 Max HP. Exactly the shape already recorded for event/hungry_for_mushrooms, where Big Mushroom's +20 Max HP lives on the event instead of the relic's after_obtained -- and the sibling relic there, Fragrant Mushroom, does it correctly, as does every other ported pickup effect. Secondary, and unobservable only because EV-2 already applies: the C# order is RelicCmd.Obtain (relic joins the player) THEN AfterObtained's LoseMaxHp, so the Cape is owned while the overflow damage resolves; the sim loses the max HP BEFORE add_relic. FLAGGED FOR THE RELIC STREAM, which owns relics/distinguished_cape.py -- this record hashes only Vakuu.cs and events/vakuu.py (rule 7).

guards.what: EV-2: the CAPE option's max-HP cost (events/vakuu.py:59 run.lose_max_hp(DistinguishedCape.MAX_HP_LOSS = 9)), whichever side of the relic/event boundary it is implemented on calls RunState.lose_max_hp (run.py:316-321), which floors max HP and CLAMPS current HP. C#'s CreatureCmd.LoseMaxHp (CreatureCmd.cs) damages the overflow through the damage pipeline (Unblockable|Unpowered) FIRST, against the UNFLOORED new max, and only then calls SetMaxHp(Math.Max(1m, newMaxHp))
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-2, one verdict at every lose_max_hp site (rule 3). Two legs, both EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes.py maxhp`): (1) the overflow is real damage, so HP-loss modifiers apply -- at 80/80 losing 10 max HP with the ported Tungsten Rod relic the sim lands on 70 and the game on 71; (2) losing more max HP than the player has: the game computes the damage against the unfloored new max (80 - 100 = -20, so 100 damage) and kills the player, while the sim floors max HP at 1 first and leaves them alive at 1/1. LIVE on leg (1): Tungsten Rod is a ported relic (relics/tungsten_rod.py:39) and every max-HP-loss event is reachable with it held. Leg (2) needs a max-HP loss larger than the player's max HP, which no ported event amount reaches, so leg (2) alone is dormant.
